rubric.note: Both direct doorway views show about 190 horizontal pixels of separation between the nearest bench edge and the frame in a 1600 px image. The central brass compass and overhead chandelier define the gathering area. The rectangular volume and small fireplace retain the earlier limitations.

From the entry the warm, changing fire is identifiable across the room. The dressed benches, candle niches and compass give the hall a distinct use, but the benches sit against separate walls and the niches lose their candles at room distance.

The close view and six-frame strip resolve overlapping soft amber tips and bright cores above the wood. The historical hero has three hard, single-tone triangles. The firebox is still faced in pale stone and the fuel reads as straight-cut timber. Floor joints, walnut and brass remain legible. The bake reports 52.54 px/m mean and 44.41 minimum.

The flame now has a hot yellow core with orange edges distinct from its surround and a warm pool immediately at the threshold. The alcove remains pale: matched hero surround L* p90 is 78.9 versus 75.9 previously. At the same hero niche the mean L* remains 22.0. The integrated floor band L* p90/p10 is 2.86 versus 2.88 previously. The floor still lacks room-scale falloff.

rubric.criterion: readability and comfort at seated VR distance
rubric.note: In the seated-camera captures the dressed benches sit to the side of each path, brass doorposts clearly frame walkable openings, and the bright fire reads from the entry. The small niche candles and subdued benches recede against the walnut. Judged from captured views only.

topFixes: Darken the firebox lining enough to silhouette the layered flames and give the straight-cut fuel a more irregular profile.
Strengthen the localized light at the niche and across the floor nearest the hearth while keeping the center lane legible.
independentScore.method: Compared the captured integration, room and fire views plus staging contact sheet against docs/art-bible.md. Used Pillow crops of the 91d9e3e doorways, close fire, strip and corresponding hero firebox at b1df5d3. Computed CIE L* from linearized sRGB at identical hero niche and surround coordinates (690,325)-(738,388) and (422,400)-(508,462); integrated floor uses every column and rows 600-929. Across five later strip panels versus the first, 5.5-12.5% of the central 295x270 fire region changes by over 12 mean absolute RGB levels. Verified evidence bytes against Git. This independent visual score is limited to the recorded captures. Owner acceptance, headset comfort and physical Quest performance require separate evidence.

rubric.note: 10x10x4 m box with coffered beam ceiling, walnut wainscot and four offset 1.6 m doors; proportions sit right for a seated 1.6 m probe. It is a plain rectangle with no alcove, niche, arch or hearth recess. The study benchmark is also a box but fills its walls with bookcases, while the hall walls are bare wallpaper above the wainscot.

Gear chandelier, brass compass floor inlay, two benches, one stained-glass lancet and two floor candelabra. That is thin for a gathering space. The template has no hearth, table or rug (hearth and rug are runtime dressing), so the floor area reads empty in p5-rooms-hall-hero.jpg.

Lightmap is clean: 68.6 px/m mean against the study's 66.3, coverage 0.742, no visible seams at the north/west door joins (seam-north, seam-west-turned). Kit-wide deduction: lightmap-only over shared tiling sets, where the study ships baked basecolor/normal/ORM from a 124,581-tri high-poly (hall high is 25,115). Walls are one repeating damask with no breakup.

Palette is on-bible: warm floor RGB 93,71,56, walnut ceiling 84,38,20, stained-glass patch on the floor. Kit/runtime deduction shared with the study (engine/diffuse frame ratio 1.90 vs study 1.89): in engine the floor shows no pools, foreground L=76 against back-floor L=77. The lightmap itself is also flatter than the study (p90/p10 texel ratio 3.96 vs 7.0).

rubric.criterion: readability and comfort at seated VR distance
rubric.note: Large clean forms, a clear enemy lane at 2-2.5 m, and a chandelier above head height. The gilt damask is high-contrast near the sconces (L p5 39 to p95 149), which is busy at the periphery.

topFixes: Add a role anchor to the template: a fireplace recess or long table zone with its own baked warm pool, so the gathering read does not depend on runtime dressing.
Break up the wall plane with bookcase or panelled bays and one niche per wall, so it matches the study's dense walls; the wallpaper should cover far less area.
Restore floor value falloff: the bake p90/p10 is 3.96 against the study's 7.0, so tighten sconce falloff and darken the corners, then fix the kit-wide engine exposure/env flattening.

rubric.note: Fixed in part: the walls are now broken into pilaster bays with moulded panels, two candle niches, a fireplace breast and a ceiling cove on the far wall (hero x 300-1060, y 230-470; p5-int-hall.jpg). That answers the old 'plain rectangle' finding. Still a 10x10 m box at one ceiling height, and the fireplace is small for the room: its surround spans hero x 422-508 (about 7% of frame width) against a 1280 px wall run, so it does not anchor the far wall. Plug check (scripts/plug.py, bbox from |in-out|>25): gilt pixels in 10 px bands on left, right and top of the former door box are 0.00% on all three bands; column-mean L* across the edges stays within 1.5 L* (left 5.6-8.7, right 9.0-10.9, top 11.5-13.8); Laplacian variance on the edges (77-81 against 66-84 inside and outside) sits inside the range of the open wall beside it, so no seam, leak, z-fight or leftover architrave.

Fixed in part: a hearth, two wall niches with candles, floor candelabra, benches and the compass inlay now give the room a gathering read; p5-int-hall.jpg shows the study through the east door with its gear column, so the hall arrives somewhere. Still thin: the niches are dim boxes (hero niche box 690-738 x 325-388: L* 22.0, p90 39.7) with a single 1-2 px candle each, and the fireplace reads as a pale tiled box rather than a lit hearth (3x crop hall-fire-3x.jpg). No table or rug in the template, so the floor centre is still empty apart from the inlay.

New faults on the new dressing. The fire is three flat cone cards of one colour with hard edges (3x crop of plug-n-in x 150-420, y 340-540), the same flat-card fault the other rooms carry. The firebox interior is pale cream stone with no soot or glow gradient: surround box 422-508 x 400-462 runs L* p10 8.7 to p90 75.9, mean RGB 129,91,61, making it the palest large surface in the room. Lightmap density fell from 68.6 to 52.5 px/m mean (report.json, min 44.4) against the study's 65.5. Damask, wainscot grain and floor stone still read cleanly.

Palette on-bible: hero frame hue 17.1, sat 0.751, L* 13.6, near the study engine hero (18.8, 0.713, 11.7). Floor value range improved: hero floor rows 470-720 L* p90/p10 6.84 (old bake figure 3.96). The in-game floor is still flat: p5-int-hall.jpg rows 600-930 give p90/p10 2.88 against 5.15 in p5-int-study.jpg. Fire colour misses candle amber: flame mask in hero x 440-495 measures RGB 213,170,127, hue 30.2, sat 0.41, R-B 86, against #F3BE65 at hue 37.4, sat 0.58, so it reads peach-cream. The left wall at hero x 0-100, y 180-400 is L* 8.8 with 46.5% of pixels under L* 5.

rubric.criterion: readability and comfort at seated VR distance
rubric.note: Large clean forms and an open 2-2.5 m lane. In-game frame has 18.2% under L* 5 and 1.9% under L* 2 (HUD masked), lower crush than the study in-game (21.8%, 7.3%). Small deduction: the pale fireplace box is the brightest large surface at eye height (L* p90 75.9) and pulls the eye from the lane.

topFixes: Rebuild the fireplace as a lit hearth: darken and soot the firebox interior (surround box L* p90 75.9 now), replace the three flat cone cards with layered soft-edged flame cards graded from a hot core to candle amber (#F3BE65; now hue 30.2, sat 0.41), and bake a warm floor pool in front of it.

Scale the fireplace up to anchor the far wall (it spans about 7% of hero width) or give it an overmantel, and make the two niches read: brighter candle and a baked warm pool inside (niche L* 22.0 now).
Restore lightmap density to the study's level (52.5 px/m mean now against 68.6 before and 65.5 in the study) and lift in-game floor falloff (p5-int-hall floor p90/p10 2.88 against the study's 5.15).
independentScoreHistory.method: Read the brief, docs/art-bible.md and the previous independentScore (68), whose findings I re-checked as claims. Weighted the engine shots: all nine docs/verification/p5-rooms-hall-*.jpg, p5-int-hall.jpg and p5-int-hall-sealed.jpg, viewed in full and as contact sheets, with 2-4x Lanczos crops of the fireplace, niches, stained lancet and the plug edges. Measured with Pillow and numpy (python3 -I, scripts in /tmp/fb17/rescore/scripts/): frame and box mean RGB, HSV hue and saturation, CIE L* mean, std, p10 and p90, share under L* 5 and 2 (HUD and button masked on p5-int shots), a flame-colour mask (R>170, G>120, R-B>60, L*>60), floor L* p90/p10, and for the plug a |in-out| diff bbox, gilt hue mask in 10 px edge bands, edge column and row L* profiles and Laplacian variance. Benchmarked against the study engine hero and p5-int-study.jpg re-measured at this build. Used report.json and engine-compare.json (lightmap vs Cycles frame ratio 0.909) only to attribute faults. The rework-2 dressing (fireplace, niches, bays, cove, candelabra) has not been approved by Paul; I scored what is visible and this score implies no approval. No repo file was edited.
